dispositions.rationale: The admit-request gate is the repository's standing rule for any new skill, recorded on the slice's work item as slice L's preamble states; a criterion restating a standing rule the tracker already evidences earns none (restraint).

Adoption beyond slice P's PR is what CR-D9 observes: the first ten merged PRs after wiring are read for a body failing the record lint, and the hook is the response. CR-G2 is the instruction and CR-P13 the first use; a criterion over future PRs' authorship is not decidable at delivery (observable-obligation, restraint).

The variant rule in section 3.1 is the section set a type carries, and the heading walk is that rule's whole decidable content; what sits under each heading is pinned type-independently by the lint criteria over the record's groups and by the four feat golden files (restraint).

'One-pager' names the region above the horizontal rule, not a word budget; the 400-word bound in CR-R1 measures that the design fits on four real PRs, and the region's parts are bounded by the record's own limits (CR-L6 sentences, one-sentence Heads-up rows, the tables' rows). A render-time word cap is a new obligation the document does not make (restraint).
CR-L1 wires a JSON Schema validator and proves it with one case per failure kind; enumerating every nested type is the schema's own job and the validator's, not a suite's (restraint).

Section 3.4 assigns this writing rule to the author and the rewrite pass and says the lint enforces only what it can decide. The rule is not mechanically decidable, and CR-W8 is the human-judgment criterion over the applied prose with a recorded basis per rule. A criterion for an undecidable rule earns none (restraint).

Each generated row carries its id beside its title or claim by the generators' stated form (CR-X1, CR-X2, CR-X5, CR-C2), so the gloss is structural in every generated group; the lint's exemption is for that reason, and a generator cannot emit a bare id (restraint).

Whether a subject identifies the component a reader would search for and states the after-state is a judgment of meaning; CR-L3 pins the decidable form (type set, component present, not a tracker id, bracketed short id, length) and CR-W8 judges the wording. A criterion for an undecidable rule earns none (restraint).

Whether the prose carries the promised content is a judgment no check over the record can decide; the form, length and required references are pinned and the content is the author's, read in review as today and judged under CR-W8 (restraint, can-fail).

In the envelope's closed disposition set the only disposition that changes code or prose is fixed; Superseded is the author's outcome word on a finding the envelope marks fixed (CR-C6), so CR-L14's condition is already the set section 3.3 names (consistency holds).

Whether a linked reviewer comment asks for a reply is a reading of the reviewer's prose, which no check can decide; requiring the URL makes the rejection traceable to a thread, and that is the decidable part (restraint).

publish calls gh with the ambient credential, the author's login; the reviewing App's token is reached only through prgroom's own code, which this skill neither imports nor invokes. Which account is logged in is a property of the session, not of the skill, and CR-D8 records the split (restraint).

The meaning check is the author's by CR-D6, which says the script cannot tell a reported check from a verified claim; CR-W8 is the human-judgment criterion that records that check against the fixtures with a basis per rule. A mechanical criterion for an undecidable check earns none (restraint).

The escalation rule is a policy the owner applies to the series the record carries (CR-W10); applying it is an owner decision outside the artifacts, which no check over them can decide (observable-obligation, restraint).

How a merge message was supplied is not observable after the fact; a message byte-identical to the record comment's render is the outcome CR-D3's flip protects, and CR-D3 states the trailer condition as the flip's evidence. The check observes the outcome the obligation exists for (observable-obligation).

scenario.given: An otherwise valid verdict envelope has a finding claim containing a fenced JSON example, and campaign copies the claim unchanged.
scenario.when: The record is generated, linted and rendered.

ground.reason: CR-D1 promises a schema-validated record. CR-L1 samples one unknown nested field and wrong types in gate exit status and reply text. It does not exercise the other nested objects and field types.

objections.objection: Schema violations in unexercised nested structures can pass lint.

scenario.expect: Every CR-L1 case passes, but lint accepts an object in a risk prose cell and an undefined property in a risk row.
scenario.given: The schema correctly constrains the tested gate, reply and nested-object cases but leaves risk-row properties permissive.
scenario.when: An author lints a record containing those untested violations.

ground.reason: Writing check 1 includes section references among the names that need a first-use gloss. CR-L2's scenarios cover tracker, criterion, decision and PR identifiers, but no section reference.

objections.objection: A bare section reference can pass every check.

scenario.expect: Lint passes while the summary refers to 'section 4.6' without explaining what it contains.
scenario.given: The identifier detector implements only CR-L2's tested identifier shapes.
scenario.when: The author lints a summary containing a section reference on first use.

ground.reason: Writing check 1 says, 'Every house term is defined where it first appears or replaced with a common word.' No check observes this requirement.

objections.objection: The artifacts can require unexplained house vocabulary.

scenario.expect: All checks pass, but a stranger encounters 'terminal-clean' in prose without a definition.
scenario.given: The prose has valid sentence counts and glosses every tested identifier.
scenario.when: The author renders a body containing an undefined house term.

ground.reason: Writing check 1 applies below the fold. CR-L2 excludes generator-owned groups, and the generator checks copy source titles and claims without checking embedded references for glosses.

objections.objection: Generated sections can reintroduce the unexplained identifiers the change promises to remove.

scenario.expect: All checks pass, but a generated finding claim first mentions D16 without a gloss.
scenario.given: A valid envelope's claim contains 'D16' and campaign preserves that claim.
scenario.when: The author generates and publishes the campaign.

ground.reason: Writing check 2 requires 'Problem, then change, then what remains' and excludes the text's drafting history. CR-L6 observes only sentence count.

objections.objection: A correctly sized summary can tell drafting history instead of the promised narrative.

scenario.expect: Lint passes, but the summary recounts successive drafts and never states what remains.
scenario.given: The summary has three sentences and satisfies the mechanical identifier and commentary checks.
scenario.when: The author renders the body.

ground.reason: Writing check 3 requires 'One clause per sentence.' Sentence-count checks do not observe clause count.

objections.objection: Multi-clause sentences can pass every check.

scenario.expect: Every check passes while the summary contains a sentence with several coordinated clauses.
scenario.given: The summary has three sentences, but one joins the problem, change and caveat with conjunctions.
scenario.when: The author lints and renders it.

ground.reason: Writing check 4 says, 'Say the number, then what it means.' No check observes that explanation or ordering.

objections.objection: Numbers can appear without their meaning.

scenario.expect: All checks pass, but a Changes sentence says only 'The result is 46.'
scenario.given: The prose contains a numeric result without its unit or interpretation.
scenario.when: The author renders the record.

ground.reason: Writing check 5 says, 'Verbs do the work.' No check observes that prose requirement.

objections.objection: The opening can retain the nominalized prose the writing contract excludes.

scenario.expect: All checks pass while Changes uses 'The implementation of validation enables the provision of enforcement.'
scenario.given: The sentence satisfies the identifier, length and commentary checks.
scenario.when: The author renders Changes.

ground.reason: Writing check 7 says, 'A caveat is a Heads-up row, not a clause.' Nonempty Heads-up validation does not establish that other prose contains no caveats.

objections.objection: A caveat can remain buried in Changes while Heads-up says None.

scenario.expect: All checks pass, but Changes contains 'The pipeline works, although older sessions can omit attribution.'
scenario.given: Heads-up contains the accepted None entry and Changes contains a caveat clause.
scenario.when: The author lints and renders the record.

ground.reason: Section 3.2 requires an after-state subject and a component readers would search for. CR-L3 checks syntax, length and metadata agreement.

objections.objection: A syntactically valid subject can fail to identify the component or resulting behavior.

scenario.expect: All subject checks pass, but the subject is 'feat(misc): do some work [9k9.484]'.
scenario.given: The record's component is misc and its subject matches that metadata.
scenario.when: The author lints the commit.

ground.reason: Section 3.2 assigns substantive purposes to Why, Change and Verification. CR-L12 checks presence, sentence counts and word counts.

objections.objection: A commit body can meet every size rule without explaining the problem, resulting change or decisive observed check.

scenario.expect: All checks pass, but the body contains generic prose and Verification names no check or observed result.
scenario.given: The three sections contain the required sentence counts and total 100 words.
scenario.when: The author lints and renders the commit message.

ground.reason: Section 3.2 says, 'No file names unless the reader must go there.' No criterion assesses that necessity.

objections.objection: Commit prose can substitute an unnecessary file inventory for an explanation.

scenario.expect: All checks pass while Change lists incidental file names that the reader need not visit.
scenario.given: The file inventory fits the required sentence and word ranges.
scenario.when: The author renders the commit.

ground.reason: Section 3.3 requires Change to contain one or two sentences. CR-L13 rejects more than two but has no zero-sentence case.

objections.objection: A reply can have an empty Change line.

scenario.expect: The reply passes the word-count and maximum-sentence checks while Change is empty.
scenario.given: Verification supplies enough words to place the whole reply within 40 to 90 words.
scenario.when: The author lints and renders that reply.

ground.reason: Section 3.3's template puts the commit at the end of Change. CR-R5 checks the absence of a parenthesis when no commit exists, but not inclusion of a supplied commit. CR-Q2 covers only prgroom's writer.

objections.objection: The standalone reply renderer can discard a supplied fix commit.

scenario.expect: Every check passes, but the rendered reply omits the commit stored in its finding entry.
scenario.given: The standalone renderer always omits commit suffixes and otherwise produces the required three lines.
scenario.when: It renders a finding entry with a commit.

ground.reason: Section 3.3 requires one reply on each finding that changed code or prose. CR-L14 uses the fixed disposition as its condition and exempts other dispositions.

objections.objection: A finding that changed code can receive no reply when its disposition is not fixed.

scenario.expect: Lint passes without a reply even though the finding caused a prose change.
scenario.given: A transferred finding caused part of its requested prose correction in this PR and deferred the remainder.
scenario.when: The author records the transferred disposition without a reply entry.

ground.reason: Section 3.3 permits a rejection reply only when a reviewer asks on the thread. CR-L13 checks the presence of a comment URL, not whether its comment contains that request.

objections.objection: An unsolicited rejection reply can pass by naming an unrelated reviewer comment.

scenario.expect: Every check passes, but the rejection reply answers a request the reviewer never made.
scenario.given: The rejection entry names a valid reviewer-comment URL whose text does not ask for a reply.
scenario.when: The author lints and posts the rendered rejection.

ground.reason: Section 3.3 requires a real change explanation and verification, and says a rejection 'gives evidence, never a bare disagreement.' Format and length checks do not observe those meanings.

objections.objection: A reply can contain unsupported assertions instead of change and verification evidence.

scenario.expect: All reply checks pass, but Verification merely repeats that the finding is wrong and provides no evidence.
scenario.given: A requested Rejected reply has the required URL, three labels and 60 words.
scenario.when: The author lints and renders it.

ground.reason: Section 3.3 says Superseded means the target no longer exists and the reply shows that it is gone. CR-R5 checks the outcome word, and CR-C6 preserves the author's selection.

objections.objection: A Superseded reply can leave the target in place and provide no evidence of its removal.

scenario.expect: All checks pass while the finding's target still exists.
scenario.given: The author selects Superseded and supplies a correctly sized, correctly formatted reply.
scenario.when: The reply is linted and rendered.

ground.reason: CR-D7 requires use of the review-verdict completeness rule and says the script 're-derives nothing.' CR-C4 substitutes the validator; CR-C5 samples completeness outcomes without substituting the completeness authority.

objections.objection: Campaign can reimplement completeness while passing the sampled cases.

scenario.expect: Every check passes, but campaign ignores a completeness-rule result on a case outside the four samples.
scenario.given: Campaign calls the schema validator but uses its own clean/advisory/mechanical/halted classifier.
scenario.when: The authoritative completeness rule rejects an otherwise schema-valid envelope for another completeness condition.

ground.reason: Section 5 says publish regenerates every generated group and refuses any differing result. CR-P1 tests one group with a recomputed stamp.

objections.objection: A generated group not exercised by that publication test can bypass regeneration.

scenario.expect: All checks pass, but publish accepts a hand-edited generated group with a recomputed stamp.
scenario.given: Publish revalidates only the group used by CR-P1's refusal case; a different generated group is edited and restamped.
scenario.when: The author publishes the record.

ground.reason: CR-D8 says record comments and replies post from the author's account. The write-call checks observe endpoints and payloads, not the authenticated posting identity.

objections.objection: The artifacts can be posted under the reviewing App or another account.

scenario.expect: Every shim check passes, but the live record comment is authored by the reviewing App.
scenario.given: gh is authenticated with the reviewing App's credentials.
scenario.when: Publish creates the record comment.

ground.reason: CR-D2 makes revisions an append-only sequence, and CR-D3 requires the newest record comment. CR-P5 and CR-P10 exercise ordering within small comment lists, not comment pagination.

objections.objection: Newest-record lookup can miss a revision on a later API page.

scenario.expect: All lookup checks pass, but merge reads an older revision.
scenario.given: The implementation reads only the first page of issue comments, and the newest marked record is on the second page.
scenario.when: Merge locates the newest record comment.

ground.reason: CR-D2 gives the record comment its own 65,536-character budget. CR-P6 tests an oversize comment and an exactly-at-limit body, but no exactly-at-limit comment.

objections.objection: Publish can reject a record comment that exactly fits its promised budget.

scenario.expect: All size checks pass, but publish refuses a 65,536-character record comment.
scenario.given: The comment-size guard rejects lengths greater than or equal to the cap, while the body guard correctly rejects only greater lengths.
scenario.when: The author publishes a record whose complete comment is exactly at the cap.

ground.reason: Section 6 says 'no suite reaches the network.' CR-L16 exercises shims and one HTTP request under proxy variables; those variables do not constrain clients that ignore them.

objections.objection: A test can reach the network while the isolation sentinels still pass.

scenario.expect: The sentinel checks pass, but another test makes a direct network connection.
scenario.given: The suite's shims and proxy-respecting HTTP sentinel behave as required, while another test uses a client with environment proxies disabled.
scenario.when: The suite runs under CR-L16's environment.

ground.reason: Section 5 says the lint reads rewritable fields from the schema 'so the allowlist and the schema cannot disagree.' CR-W1 and CR-W3 test the current list without changing its annotations.

objections.objection: A hard-coded rewrite allowlist can silently diverge from the schema.

scenario.expect: All current-list checks pass, but extract-prose and apply-prose continue admitting a field after its schema annotation is removed.
scenario.given: The implementation hard-codes the presently correct allowlist.
scenario.when: A copied schema removes x-rewritable from an otherwise unchanged field.

ground.reason: CR-D6 assigns meaning checks to the author: each diff is read for a strengthened claim, dropped exception or erased deferred work. Instruction-file presence and structural application checks do not observe that author action.

objections.objection: A structurally valid rewrite can be applied without the required semantic review.

scenario.expect: Every check passes, but an accepted replacement strengthens the claim without author review.
scenario.given: A replacement changes 'the gate reported exit 0' to 'the change is verified' while preserving protected values.
scenario.when: The author applies the response without reading the diff.

ground.reason: Section 7 assigns the owner 'reading four applied diffs.' CR-W8's check observes an evidence row naming the owner, date, revision and correction count; it does not observe the required review or its judgments.

objections.objection: The wiring can proceed with recorded review metadata but without the owner's actual applied-diff review.

scenario.expect: All checks pass while the owner has not read the four applied diffs.
scenario.given: The evidence row contains the required metadata, but no owner judgment has been obtained.
scenario.when: The slice is treated as delivered.

ground.reason: CR-D6 specifies comparisons over successive ten-PR windows and escalation first to medium effort and then to gpt-6.1-sol. Counts and pin-file agreement do not check those decisions.

objections.objection: The rewrite model can remain unchanged after the specified escalation trigger.

scenario.expect: All checks pass, but the next window still uses gpt-6-luna at low effort.
scenario.given: The mean correction count on PRs six to ten equals the mean on PRs one to five, and all counts are correctly recorded.
scenario.when: The next ten-PR window starts.

ground.reason: CR-D3 says five merges have used the merge command before the settings flip. CR-G3 compares resulting messages; identical messages do not establish use of that command.

objections.objection: The settings can flip without evidence that five merges used the required workflow.

scenario.expect: CR-G3 passes, but none of the five merges used the merge subcommand.
scenario.given: The owner supplied byte-identical rendered messages manually through gh on five consecutive merges.
scenario.when: The settings are changed after those merges.

ground.reason: Section 6 promises 'Eight slices, each one pull request.' No check observes the delivery partition.

objections.objection: The implementation can ship as a combined change rather than the promised incremental slices.

scenario.expect: All functional and artifact checks pass, but several slices land in one PR.
scenario.given: L, R, X, C, P and Q are implemented and verified together.
scenario.when: The author delivers their combined branch.

ground.reason: Section 7 states slice dependencies and requires W's item to take a dependency edge on the owner-ruling item. No check observes that tracker edge or the full landing order.

objections.objection: The declared dependency structure can be absent despite passing implementation checks.

scenario.expect: All checks pass, but W's tracker item has no dependency edge on the decision item.
scenario.given: The ruling was obtained before the recorded runs, but the required tracker dependency was never created.
scenario.when: The rewrite slice is delivered.

ground.reason: Section 7 assigns live context and campaign runs and a real-PR dry run to owner vetting. The corresponding checks use shims or synthetic output rather than observing those owner tasks.

objections.objection: The specified owner vetting can be skipped while all suites pass.

scenario.expect: All checks pass, but the owner has performed none of the specified live comparisons.
scenario.given: X, C and P pass their recorded-fixture suites.
scenario.when: Those slices are delivered without the live work-item run, captured-PR comparison or real-PR dry run.

ground.reason: Slice P's introduction promises a dry run 'printing the comment and body it would write.' CR-P12 checks only the marker line and the body's first heading.

objections.objection: Dry-run output can be incomplete or differ from the actual publication payload.

scenario.expect: CR-P12 passes, but stdout contains only a marker and a heading.
scenario.given: The dry-run implementation prints those two tokens and makes no GitHub calls.
scenario.when: The author previews publication.

ground.reason: Outside its acceptance criteria, the document does not commit to a particular exit status, diagnostic or atomic failure policy for an unknown tracker item. CR-X4 discharges no inventoried part.

objections.objection: CR-X4 introduces an unknown-item failure contract without an obligation in the surrounding document.

scenario.expect: The check runs, but no stated document obligation depends on its required nonzero exit, named diagnostic and unchanged record.
scenario.given: The supplied work-item id does not exist.
scenario.when: CR-X4 checks context's response.

ground.reason: CR-W8's stated check observes review metadata. The surrounding document promises actual owner vetting, not that metadata artifact itself, so the check discharges no inventory part.

objections.objection: The evidence-row check can pass independently of every promised owner-review outcome.

scenario.expect: The metadata check succeeds while no document obligation depends on those fields alone.
scenario.given: An evidence row names an owner, date, revision and correction count but contains no completed owner review.
scenario.when: CR-W8's stated evidence-row check runs.

ground.reason: Read as written, CR-L10's clause for docs, chore, build, ci, style and revert records ('fails with one or with more than one risk row') cannot hold in the same record as CR-L4 ('a risk table with no row fails lint'), section 3.1's docs variant ('a one-row Risk table') or CR-R1's docs and chore fixtures (which render a Risk heading): under the literal reading no record of these six types can pass lint at any row count, and the two plausible readings demand opposite lints.

objections.objection: For the six reduced-scope types the criteria leave no satisfiable risk-row count. CR-L10 as worded fails a docs record with one or more risk rows; CR-L4 fails any record with none; section 3.1 and CR-R1 require exactly one. An implementer reading the clause as 'zero rows' and one reading it as 'exactly one row' (the apparent intent, with a missing 'without' or 'fewer than') ship lints that accept and reject the same record.

scenario.expect: Under the literal reading, lint fails the record for having one risk row; deleting the row makes CR-L4 fail it for having none, so no docs, chore, build, ci, style or revert record can pass; under the exactly-one reading the same record passes. The two readings gate each other's suites red on the same fixture.
scenario.given: A docs-type record whose risk table holds exactly one row, the form section 3.1's docs variant and CR-R1's docs and chore fixtures require.
scenario.when: lint runs over the record and CR-L10's per-type case is judged against CR-L4's and CR-R1's.

ground.reason: CR-L2 names exactly two gloss scopes — the body and each reply, 'since a reply is read alone' — and leaves the commit message's scope undecided, but the commit prose renders both into the body's Proposed-commit-message fold and standalone into git log as the merge commit, so the two readings pass and fail the same record.

objections.objection: Whether the commit message's prose fields belong to the body's gloss scope or are a scope of their own is left open. A record whose summary glosses an id that commit.why then uses bare passes lint under the first reading and fails under the second. Under the first, the merged commit — the artifact CR-P8 and CR-G3 exist to control — carries the unglossed first mention that section 1 names as the problem. The decision blocked: which scope the commit prose is linted in, deciding whether git-log readers get glosses.

scenario.expect: Read as body scope, lint passes and git log shows a merged commit whose Why section carries the bare id; read as its own scope (the reply precedent, since a commit is read alone in git log), lint fails the record until the commit prose glosses the id. The record is either accepted or rejected depending on a reading the criterion never states.
scenario.given: A record whose summary glosses the tracker id 9k9.484 on first use and whose commit.why uses 9k9.484 bare.
scenario.when: lint runs, and the PR then merges through the merge subcommand so the rendered commit message becomes the merge commit.

ground.reason: CR-L16 requires the whole suite to run and pass under a PATH holding only the shim directory and the interpreter, while CR-R3's check runs git interpret-trailers over the rendered fixtures; the criteria state no git shim and no exemption for assertion-time tools, so in one suite the two cannot both hold as worded.

objections.objection: The skill ships one test file discovered by content-tests, so CR-L16's environment and CR-R3's check share a run. If 'the suite runs under' that restricted PATH covers the test process, git is not findable and CR-R3's interpret-trailers assertion fails, so the suite does not pass and CR-L16 fails. The reconciliation — the restriction applies only to the code under test, with the harness invoking git by absolute path or a pass-through shim — is a reading the criteria leave to the implementer, and the two readings produce a suite that passes and one that cannot.

scenario.expect: With the PATH applied to the whole test process, the git invocation fails to spawn and CR-R3's case errors out, so the suite fails under CR-L16's environment; with the PATH scoped to the invoked script, the same case passes. Which scope the runner's PATH governs decides whether the R-slice criteria are satisfiable at all.
scenario.given: The skill's suite, containing CR-R3's check that runs git interpret-trailers on each fixture's rendered commit message, executed by CR-L16's runner, which sets PATH to the shim directory and the interpreter only.
scenario.when: content-tests runs the suite under CR-L16's environment.

ground.reason: CR-P7 states exhaustively that the only GitHub writes publish makes are one issue comment create and one PR body edit (decision CR-D8 states the same list), while CR-P14 has publish --create also open the pull request, so in the create circumstance the two criteria require incompatible write sets unless CR-P7 is silently read as exempting the create mode — an exemption its text never states.

objections.objection: CR-P7's obligation and CR-P14's specified behavior cannot both hold in one publish --create run: the call log holds a gh pr create besides the comment create and body edit, three writes where CR-P7 permits two. CR-P7's own check (no review, review comment or comment edit call) passes either way, so the obligation and the check diverge, and whether the exhaustive list binds the create path is left open — deciding whether PR creation may sit on publish as a flag or must be a separate verb the criteria never name.

scenario.expect: The shim's log holds three writes against CR-P7's two. Read as exhaustive, CR-P7 is violated by the run CR-P14 specifies, and an implementer must move PR creation off publish; read as steady-state only, the same run satisfies both. The criteria admit both verdicts on the same log.
scenario.given: A record with no PR number, and a gh shim recording every call.
scenario.when: publish --create runs per CR-P14: gh pr create, then the record comment, then the PR body edit.

ground.reason: CR-P3 repairs a publish interrupted between its two writes, but CR-P14's --create is a four-step sequence — gh pr create, post the record comment, set the body, write the PR number into the record — with the number written last. No criterion covers an interruption anywhere before that final step, so the failure path of the one command the skill names as the way a PR is opened is untested.

objections.objection: A publish --create that dies after gh pr create succeeds leaves a live PR and a record that still holds no PR number; the criteria let the rerun open a duplicate PR for one change instead of adopting the existing one.

scenario.expect: the rerun adopts the existing PR, or refuses naming it, rather than calling gh pr create again; no criterion checks either outcome, and as written the rerun opens a second PR
scenario.given: a record with no PR number, on a branch that already has an open PR created by an earlier publish --create that stopped before writing the number back
scenario.when: the author reruns publish --create

ground.reason: CR-L4 makes the record state emptiness explicitly for heads_up, discovered and risk, and CR-L10 requires a criteria group for feat-class records — but neither makes a present-but-empty criteria table a failure (a verification group holding no gates and no not-run entries has the same hole). The zero-row case passes both criteria as written.

objections.objection: The lint accepts a feat record whose criteria group is present but holds no rows, so a PR delivered against no criteria publishes a body whose Criteria section is an empty table.

scenario.expect: lint fails naming the empty group; no criterion checks this, and as written both lint and render pass
scenario.given: a record of type feat whose criteria group is present and holds an empty list
scenario.when: lint runs, then render

ground.reason: CR-P8 renders the merge commit message from the newest record comment and refuses only on a lint --pr failure or a missing comment; CR-P5 finds the comment by marker and CR-P11 defines the digest, but no criterion validates the comment's folded record against its schema or its marker digest before it is trusted. CR-D8 stops the pipeline editing comments it did not post; nothing checks a comment that was edited or truncated by someone else.

objections.objection: A newest record comment whose folded JSON is malformed or no longer matches its marker digest reaches merge unvalidated, and its content becomes a permanent merge commit's message.

scenario.expect: a refusal naming the comment before any merge call; no criterion checks this, and as written the render either crashes or commits the corrupted text
scenario.given: a PR whose newest record comment was edited so its fold no longer parses, or so its content no longer matches the digest in its marker line
scenario.when: merge runs on that PR
